body:
## Why

The coordinator asks for comfortable driving hours and rest days during discovery, before the trip has a shape. On a short trip, the answer often doesn't matter yet, and the user has nothing to judge it against until they see each day's drive. So the question feels out of place, and asking it again each turn makes that worse. The answer starts to matter once a day's drive gets long, which the sketches' road times and the daily driving check (technical spec 8) show.

## What happened

Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix. The trip is a 4-day loop from Natick, MA to Bar Harbor, with one long drive up on Day 1 and short drives home.

- The coordinator asked about driving hours, scenic or fastest, and a day with no driving in turns 1, 2, 3, and 4. Joe left them unanswered on purpose. It didn't hold up the plan to get an answer, which was better than in earlier sessions.
- In turn 5 the user said: "our longest drive is going to be [Natick] to Bar Harbor, and that's fine. So that's like, you know, we expected a kind of long day that day. The rest are shorter. [...] So I think we're good on driving."

Joe's read: on this trip the answer should have been worked out from the plan, not asked up front. By turn 4 the user had seen the sketches and agreed to the route with each day's drive time, so asking for hours was only ticking a box. It's the second session where the question felt unnatural. The coordinator also asked about rest days four times, and then dropped it. Asking again and again, then giving up, isn't a good way to find the answer. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-30.

- In turn 12 the user picked Pemaquid Point for Saturday, knowing it added about an hour. Saturday became 5 h 36 m of driving with the drive buffer (turn span `a524f4d65cf4c50d`). The coordinator said "That's about 5½ hours of driving with breaks, a long day but under your 6." The 6 was the number it set itself in turn 5 to cover Day 1 (see #167). The user never said 6 hours was normal, and had expected the days home to be about 3½ to 4 hours. Under a 4-hour default, Saturday would have warned, and the coordinator would have asked whether 5½ hours is OK.

#167 is about what to set once the user answers vaguely. This issue is about when to ask.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 5.2: comfortable driving hours is required, and rest days aren't.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (the coordinator's instructions for the trip brief and comfortable driving hours), section 8 (a check that compares against a trip brief item is skipped while that item is empty), and section 10 (the recommended daily driving, 6 hours).

## Open questions

- ~~How does the coordinator find out the comfortable driving hours? Joe's idea: never suggest a day over 6 hours of driving on its own. When a day goes over 4 hours, ask the user whether that's OK, and whether it's a normal amount for them. If they want 8 or 10 hours, that's fine, up to the maximum of 12. So it comes up only when a day needs it. Proposal: make 4 hours the default for comfortable driving hours, as 8:00 a.m. is for the usual start time. The daily driving check then runs from the start, and its warning on a day over 4 hours is the cue to ask. A yes approves that day (as in #167), or raises the default when it's normal for them. The recommended daily driving, 6 hours, becomes the most the coordinator suggests without the user asking. On this trip, the user would have been asked twice: about Day 1's 5½ hours, and about Saturday's 5½ hours once Pemaquid Point was added.~~ Settled 2026-10-30, in chat, as proposed:
  - Comfortable driving hours starts at 4 hours, as the usual start time starts at 8:00 a.m. The 4 is a new setting in technical spec section 10, the default comfortable driving hours. The trip brief shows it as the default until the user says otherwise.
  - So the daily driving check runs from the start. Its warning on a day over the comfortable driving hours is the coordinator's cue to ask whether that day is OK, and whether that much driving is normal for the user.
  - "That day is fine" gives the day a drive hours approval. "That's normal for us" raises the trip brief's comfortable driving hours, and is saved to user memory as a standing preference.
  - The coordinator never suggests a day over the recommended daily driving, 6 hours, on its own. The user can ask for more, up to the maximum daily driving, 12 hours.
  - The coordinator doesn't ask about driving hours during discovery.
- ~~Should rest days leave the trip brief? Joe's idea: they should come up in the conversation when they fit, not as a question every trip gets. The trip brief acts as a checklist the coordinator works through. On a 5-night trip with 5 stays, asking for a day with no driving makes no sense. Proposal: remove `restDaysText` from the trip brief. A wish such as "one day off in Moab" goes in trip memory. Marking a day as a rest day with `update_day` stays as it is.~~ Settled 2026-10-30, in chat, as proposed:
  - Remove `restDaysText` from the trip brief: the domain code, `update_trip_brief`'s input, the coordinator's instructions, and the saved form.
  - A wish such as "one day off in Moab" goes to trip memory, like any other wish for this trip. A standing habit, such as "we always take a day off mid-trip", goes to user memory.
  - Marking a day as a rest day with `update_day` stays as it is.
  - The coordinator offers a rest day only when the trip calls for one: a trip of about a week or more, or several long driving days in a row. Otherwise it comes up only when the user raises it.
  - Every saved trip holds `restDaysText`, empty or not, and the saved form is checked strictly, so a one-line migration removes the key from every saved trip, as `migrations/0008_drop_stay_tier_nights.sql` did. Nothing is carried over: the one trip Joe cares about, Bar Harbor, has no rest days.

## Do

- Change functional spec 5.2, technical spec 5.2 and 10, and the domain model to match the answers. Remove `restDaysText` from the trip brief's code, its tool input, and its saved form.
- Add a migration that removes `restDaysText` from the trip brief in every saved trip's plan, as `migrations/0008_drop_stay_tier_nights.sql` does for its keys.
- Add the default comfortable driving hours setting, 4 hours, to the settings and technical spec section 10. A new trip's trip brief starts with it, as it starts with the usual start time.
- **Ask first the questions the trip sketches need.** In turn 1, the coordinator's reply asked 7 numbered questions, though the instructions say "Ask a few questions at a time." Joe answered the ones the sketches needed, and the sketches in turn 2 came out well. Have the coordinator ask first the few questions it needs to offer the trip sketches, and the rest later. Raised by Joe. Moved here from #231 on 2026-10-30, since it also decides which questions discovery asks, and when. Write it together with dropping driving hours and rest days from discovery, so the two read as one rule.
- Change the coordinator's instructions in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`, and the `update_trip_brief` description if the default changes what it says. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.

## Done when

- The coordinator's instructions say when to raise driving hours and rest days, and to ask first the questions the trip sketches need. The design docs match.
- A trip saved before the change loads after `npm run migrate`, run locally.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
